author: felicepantaleo
body:
`CachingAllocator::tryReuseCachedBlock` assigns the cached block descriptor over the descriptor of the new allocation, and then restores the queue. This also replaces `block.requested` with the size requested by the previous allocation that used the block. `cacheStatus().requested` therefore reports the sizes of earlier allocations. Almost every allocation is served from the cache, so the value is wrong whenever it is read.

The counter stays internally consistent, because `free()` subtracts the same value that `allocate()` added. There is no leak and no drift. Only the reported size is wrong.

The function now takes from the cached block only what the cache owns, which is the buffer, the event and the bin size. The queue, the bin and the requested size of the new allocation stay in place. The bug is no longer possible to write, instead of being corrected after the fact. Any field added to `BlockDescriptor` in the future is also safe.

The block is taken out of the cache with `extract` before it is modified. The accounting is updated after the operations that can throw. On master, if the insertion into `liveBlocks_` throws, the same buffer is left owned by both maps, and a later `free()` of that pointer subtracts zero bytes. This is only reachable on `bad_alloc`, and it is now closed.

One of the two copies of the block descriptor per reuse is removed. Each copy touches three `std::optional` of alpaka handles.

Both `TODO` comments in the function are resolved.

### Test

`HeterogeneousCore/AlpakaInterface/test/testCachingAllocator.cc` allocates 300 bytes and 500 bytes from the same 512 byte bin, and checks the reported sizes. The test runs on the host device and needs no accelerator.

On master the test fails.
title: CachingAllocator: report the current requested size in reused block
